newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Gazprom cuts supplies to Ukraine.
newsitem.headline: Russian Gazprom cuts supplies to Ukraine.

text.p: Russia's Gazprom natural gas monopoly said on Tuesday it had cut gas supplies to Ukraine by one third because of debts for unpaid supplies.
"Supplies have been reduced by one third to 40 million cubic meters a day as of today," Gazprom spokesman Sergei Smirnov said.
He said the move would not affect supplies of Russian gas shipped across Ukraine to Europe.
Smirnov said earlier on Tuesday Gazprom had cut deliveries to Belarus by one half over Minsk's $125.5 million in debts for supplies. He had no figure for the amount owed by Kiev.
The cuts are a sign that Gazprom, the world's largest natural gas producer, will no longer tolerate nonpayment by former Soviet customers.

Gazprom, Russia's largest corporate tax payer, is under pressure by the government to contribute more to the budget. It had fallen behind on tax payments earlier this year because it was owed vast amounts by customers both at home and in the former Soviet Union.
